voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: At seventy-one, Ambrose Bierce, the writer they called Bitter Bierce, set out for revolutionary Mexico. He never came home.
He reportedly went to travel with Pancho Villa's army as an observer.
His last known letter is dated Chihuahua, December twenty-sixth, nineteen thirteen. He was leaving, it said, for an unknown destination.
After that, nothing certain. Some say he was at Ojinaga, on the border, in January nineteen fourteen. Others say Sierra Mojada, or Marfa, Texas.
Civil War veteran, author of The Devil's Dictionary. Where and when he died has never been established.
